title: Ops Playlet Sandbox: Gating + Telemetry Hypervisor
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a sandboxed execution surface ("playlet sandbox") and a lightweight telemetry hypervisor that enforces gating policies before runbooks-as-tasks are allowed to execute against prod-adjacent systems. Goal: let first-line support safely run idempotent admin utilities while capturing minimal, structured telemetry for regressions and SLOs. Scope: sandbox controller, gating rules engine, telemetry adapter, RBAC integration, and a canary rollout path for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox controller can launch playlets in a restricted namespace with ephemeral credentials and timeboxed sessions
Gating engine evaluates policy rules (quota, risk score, approval state) and blocks or allows execution with auditable decision logs
Telemetry hypervisor emits structured events (playlet_id, user_id, input_hash, decision, latency) to Ops stream and to Console dashboards
Rollback safety: any playlet flagged as unsafe is automatically aborted and circuit opens for 30m; team can configure thresholds
Integration tests (unit + e2e) demonstrate that a simulated dangerous action is prevented and logged

decisions: Opted for ephemeral container sandboxes over WASM for first iteration because we can reuse existing infra and have clearer isolation guarantees
Telemetry will be minimal and structured (no raw user inputs persisted) to reduce PII risk — input hashes only
Gating evaluation is synchronous in the control plane to preserve auditability; long-running playlets will move to async approval path
Warm-pool approach chosen to reduce cold-start latency; pool size is configurable per-tenant
tradeoffs: Using containers increases resource cost vs lightweight runtimes but simplifies isolation and permissioning (short-term win)
Synchronous gating adds ~30-80ms to median request latency; mitigated by warm-pool and local-cache of frequent decisions
Restricting telemetry reduces utility for debugging but lowers compliance burden — tradeoff accepted for GA
risks: Telemetry pipeline lag could cause decision mismatches — mitigated by blocking new sessions when lag threshold exceeded
Warm-pool resources could be misused if per-tenant quotas are misconfigured — monitoring + alerts required
Complex policy language increases risk of misconfiguration — policy editor UX must make common cases simple
qa_plan: Unit tests for rule evaluator and policy parser
Integration tests that simulate playlets performing allowed and disallowed actions
Chaos test: drop telemetry events for 5-10m and validate fail-safe blocks new executions
User acceptance: 5 internal support engineers run a curated suite of playlets and sign off
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal support (5 users) for 2 weeks
Phase 2: limited internal product teams (50 users) with monitoring thresholds
Phase 3: enable for all support and Dedicated customers with opt-in policy
Auto-roll-back trigger: any 3 safety breaches within 48h or telemetry pipeline lag > 5m
